analysis.title: GS Abbas - GS US Daily Download 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: Foreign investors own 18% of the US equity market versus 2% for hedge funds. Their positioning has stayed just below the 50th percentile since 2009.

GS estimates AI demand adds to core PCE through four channels. Software and accessories add roughly 20bp, but most of that is judged to be mismeasurement. Electronics input costs add about 15bp in total until late next year. Data center power demand adds 5-10bp to core and another 5-10bp to headline. Industrial metals add about 5bp to core.

Digital Ads Q3 preview: debates on Alphabet and Meta center on AI capex, capital intensity, funding needs and positioning in consumer agents. GS sees both with a right to win at the platform layer if they execute. Investors are more comfortable with current ROIC on prior spending. Questions remain about the 2028-2030 revenue and EBIT needed to earn returns on 2026/2027 capex.

AMAT: GS came away incrementally positive from the Investor Breakfast at SEMICON West and the EPIC Center unveiling (Oct 12-13). The stock fell 7% in a sector-wide selloff, possibly on the lack of a medium-term WFE forecast and an earnings target before 2030. GS expects a recovery because earnings season should validate higher 2028 earnings power from WFE growth and deposition/etch exposure.

Payments preview: GS is broadly positive heading into 3Q earnings. Spending volumes are robust and September trends stayed strong. Regulatory and disruption risks are fading, and agentic commerce is emerging as a growth driver for carded payments. The group is seen as insulated from higher rates, higher inflation and AI disruption, and is inexpensive versus its history after years of multiple compression.
Payments stock picks: V, MA, TOST and GLBE are highlighted. Into earnings GS is more constructive on V, MA, PYPL, GLBE and RSKD, and more cautious on FIS, FISV and FOUR.

JPM 3Q26 results: EPS $5.57 reported versus GSe $6.10 and Visible Alpha consensus $5.92. Core EPS was $6.05 versus GSe $6.28 and consensus $6.04. Core ROTCE was 21.5%, about 4.5pp above the 17% medium-term guide.

JPM guidance: 2027 NII ex Markets of about $107bn (+10% YoY) versus Street $103.1bn. GS believes total 2027 NII of $115bn+ is supported, though management said the range of outcomes is wider than normal. With 2027 consensus expenses of about $114bn confirmed as roughly right, GS sees about $4bn (4%) of 2027 PPNR upside versus the Street.
GS changed its JPM estimates: 2026E/28E PPNR -2%/+1%, and EPS down 2%/2%/3% on lower buybacks.

Market update: the index was rangebound but there was heavy rotation underneath. Semis fell for a fifth straight session, with memory down 4%. MU and SNDK are lower in 7 of 8 sessions. Many cited China's CXMT claims of a memory chip breakthrough, but GS sees it more as a cooling of the 'AI bottleneck' trades globally.

Tech squeezes continued (INFY, SaaS, HPQ). Mag 7 and the QUALITY factor stayed firm. The GS Cycs v Defs pair fell in 6 of 7 sessions. Banks were mixed after earnings, with an early move down tied to higher rates and the sector likely being a funding short for weakness in the AI trade.

Flows: floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale. Hedge funds were moderate net buyers, driven by macro products. Long-only flows skewed slightly to sale, driven by tech. Generalist and long-only outflows from Tech/AI/Memory continued, with money largely rotating out of the sector. Macro and non-traditional financials supply picked up. Volumes were tracking -14% versus the 20-day average.
